issues.description: Task intent is incoherent — 'Intent' field is a comma-separated keyword dump (alter, blocks, build, duplicate, eliminate, etc.) with no grammatical structure or actionable goal
Missing failure context — 'Touched files from prior run: unknown' and 'Prior commit SHA: unknown' prevent identifying what was attempted and why it failed
Contradictory acceptance criteria — 'preserve existing behavior' and 'code modification count remains unchanged' conflict with 'remove duplicate pricinggridreconstruction' which requires deletions

Security concern left unresolved — spec warns of 'allowlist without proper authentication or authorization checks, potentially exposing the system' but does not specify whether this is a bug to fix or inadvertently introduced

Cross-repo patch transplant without context — references to pareto-2080, beethoven/recover-missing-branch-relfix, and prediction-markets-institute branches are unvetted; similarity scores (0.253–0.515) suggest significant drift
Mysterious requirements — 'preserve e string in updated files' is opaque; no prior mention of what 'e string' refers to or why it matters
Task routing confusion — references to 'pareto-2080', 'beethoven', 'prediction-markets-institute' in a task for 'apparently-law' project; unclear which repo is the target
Truncated prior patch — 'Prior patch diff (truncated)' offers only a security note and no actual code changes, making it impossible to rebuild or adapt

suggestions: Rewrite intent section as a single, clear sentence: e.g., 'Remove duplicate PricingGridReconstruction logic from X and Y files while maintaining behavior compatibility'
Inspect the branch/worktree first: run `git log -1 --name-only` on the existing shadow-004b83eb-cowork branch to recover what was touched and when
Clarify acceptance criteria conflict: if removing duplicates is the goal, update the 'code modification count' criterion to specify 'lines removed' rather than 'unchanged'

Separate security from refactoring: clarify whether the allowlist auth bug is in-scope for this task or a known acceptable technical debt; if in-scope, add it as a separate bullet in the acceptance criteria
Validate source patches: before adapting pareto-2080 or beethoven patches, confirm they exist, are accessible, and target the same file/module as apparently-law
Define the 'e string' requirement: provide a grep pattern or file:line reference so the coder knows what to preserve
Provide a minimal reproduction: include a test case or concrete example of the duplicate code that needs removal
Re-anchor to apparently-law: clarify the target branch in the apparently-law repo and confirm it is not a stale/orphaned task specification
missing_context: Concrete goal: what exactly is being fixed/built? (e.g., 'remove duplicate PricingGridReconstruction'?)
Which files are involved (currently listed only as 'pricinggridreconstruction' keyword)
Complete prior patch diff showing the failed implementation
Prior commit SHA or worktree path to inspect existing work
Clear failure message: what test or build step failed and how?
Security bug details: is the auth-less allowlist a regression in this task or pre-existing?
Definition of 'e string' and why it must be preserved
Accessibility and relevance of source repos (pareto-2080, beethoven, prediction-markets-institute) to apparently-law
Clear test or acceptance proof (currently unverifiable)
ai_review.merge_risk_reason: Task is an agentic repair attempt with incomplete prior context, contradictory requirements (preserve count vs. remove duplicates), unresolved security concern (allowlist without auth), and references to unvalidated external patches. Cross-repo patch transplant without coherent goal or test cases creates high risk of introducing bugs, breaking existing behavior, or exacerbating security issues. The 'Acceptance' criterion about an 'e string' is unexplained and may mask a hidden constraint. Recommend blocking merge until task spec is rewritten with concrete file targets, failure reproduction, and clear go/no-go criteria.

pre_generated_tests.notes: The task spec is corrupted or unintelligible: Intent text is garbled, source patches are not provided, prior artifacts show unknown touched files and missing prior commit SHA. Cannot generate meaningful tests without: (1) Clear description of what functionality is being implemented, (2) Actual source files or reproducible prior run state, (3) Specific behavior requirements beyond vague 'preserve existing behavior'
